title: 2026-11-16 — Shape a live probe of a transient CLI screen before its starts are counted

data.head: ## 2026-11-16 — Shape a live probe of a transient CLI screen before its starts are counted

body:
A live probe that waits for a screen the CLI shows only for a moment (the forced session-feedback survey on 2.1.325)
spends capped starts on its own shape unless three things are known first: what makes the screen appear and when, what
closes it, and who holds the wheel at the moment the key lands. Here half the founder's cap went that way. One start
looked only after `turn-ended`, by which time the survey had come and gone. A driver send typing over the input box
closed the survey within about half a second. A turn started from the child's argument was filed as the human's, so the
wheel was the human's before any key. Read those three from the CLI bundle and the wrapper's code, and rehearse the
order against the fake agent, before the first counted start; a start then measures the product, not the rig.

The session closes a chunk whose feature was dropped: a key answering the claude CLI's session-feedback survey was to be exempted from taking the wheel, and it is not built.
The exemption was written and went green in an earlier run, then rolled back to the committed state on the founder's ruling; no product, test or fixture file changed and no symbol, schema, dependency or gate changed.
What it adds is a record only: the survey's screen grammar on claude 2.1.325 measured live over six starts, and two findings about the start's shape (a driver send typed over the input box closes the forced survey; an argument-started turn is filed as human-origin).
The capability is deferred to a later version on the founder's word; the rule that run never reads screen content, transport-only for an unverified CLI and the closed non-editing stdin list all stand unwidened.
The rule that a human key takes the wheel stands with no exception: a key answering the survey still takes the wheel like any other human keystroke, since the exemption was not built.
The closed list of non-editing stdin input the classifier ignores stays closed: the survey answer key was not added to it.
The rule that no screen content is parsed beyond signatures stands unwidened: the wheel is not taught the survey screen.
The rule that the boundary check never inspects claude content is affirmed: no survey literal is read by the boundary.
The rule that live readings never gate is exercised: six live starts were recorded as evidence and gate nothing.

The rule that a send is refused while the human types is the reading of the sixth start (second send refused as human typing), because an argument-started turn is filed as human-origin; the rule stands unchanged.
The rule that terminal sequences are not human editing stands as written; the survey key joins no non-editing class.
CLI output discipline, refusal format, hint and unable lines, exit codes and the --json failure documents: no output string or code moved.
The viola list board, its captions, colour and SGR rules, NAME truncation and stale-row dimming.
CI integration, the a11y gate, coverage and mutation audit, zero flakiness and the test counts: the gate set and its suites are unchanged.
Screen-reader targets and the manual keyboard and Orca passes.
Link, unlink, revive, plugin install, hook call, MCP frame tool and socket or strict-modes refusals.
The absences (web or graphical frontend, touch surface, internationalization, rendered page, user time limit) and the scope and tier decisions.

The session closed as a record chunk: no product, test or fixture file differs from the commit it started on.
A survey exemption (a key answering the claude CLI's session-feedback survey keeps the wheel with the driver) was written and green in an earlier run, then rolled back whole and never committed, on the founder's ruling to drop the feature.
What it measured on claude 2.1.325, in six live starts kept as evidence only: the forced survey's screen grammar, and two findings about the start's shape.
Finding one: a driver send typed over the input box closes the forced survey; the survey literals stood at most 535 ms.
Finding two: a turn started by an argument at start is filed with origin human, so a second driver send is refused as human-typing.
Nothing was added or retired: no ledger row, no verify run, no recorded screen, no fake-agent option, no test; the survey capability is deferred, not built.
The rule that run never reads screen content stands unwidened: the survey exemption that would have had the wheel classifier match a survey screen was withdrawn, so no exception to it exists.
The transport-only degrade on an unverified CLI stands unwidened: no survey behaviour was admitted on an unverified version.

The per-behaviour CLI capability ledger and the ledger as the single gate for CLI behaviour: no survey ledger row was added, and the planned carry for one on the 2.1.325 recorded fixture set was withdrawn.
The closed list of non-editing bytes: a key answering the survey did not join it; the list is unchanged.

The wheel's byte-source claim, the human always winning the wheel, and the wheel classifier only observing: a key typed while the survey shows still claims the wheel for the human as any human byte does; the session confirms that rule rather than excepting it.
Screen signatures as compiled literals and screen fixtures keeping only signature rows: no survey literal and no recorded survey screen were added.
No probe for a shape no send relies on, and verify's bounded child set: no verify run for a forced survey was added, since no send relies on the survey.

The prompt-submitted event's origin: a turn started by a start argument is measured to be filed origin human; a row on prompt-submitted origin or on harness prompts not being a human take may be checked against that reading.
The human-typing refusal reason: a driver send after an argument-started turn was refused human-typing, the existing refusal, unchanged.
Real CLI probes run only locally and no live claude in CI: the six live starts ran locally and recorded nothing into fixtures.

The session changed no product, test or fixture file: a survey exemption written in an earlier run was rolled back to the committed bytes and never committed.
It closes as a record only: the session-feedback survey grammar of claude 2.1.325 was measured in six live starts, and the founder ruled the feature dropped.
The wheel is not taught the survey: a key answering the survey still counts as human typing, and the stdin classifier's closed non-editing list is not widened.
Two shape facts were measured and not built on: a driver send typed over the input box closes the forced survey, and an argument-started turn is filed as human origin.
No symbol, channel method, event, env var read, dependency, config key, fixture or recorded screen was added, and no count moved.
The planned survey capability-ledger row, verify run, recorded screen, fake-agent survey option and wheel test were all withdrawn; the cap is deferred.
The stdin classifier's closed non-editing list stands unwidened: the survey is measured but deliberately not added, so the list's membership is unchanged.
The rule that the non-editing list holds measured replies only is confirmed: a measured reply was still kept off the list by the founder's ruling, not by lack of measurement.
Human typing takes the wheel: a key answering the survey keeps taking the wheel from the driver, unchanged.
The send refusal human-typing and the wheel event cause human-input stand as they are; a live start read a second send refused as human typing after the survey key.
The unverified CLI gate (an unverified CLI is transport only) stands unwidened by the founder's word.
Verify reads screens only by signatures against compiled literals: no survey literal and no verify run for a forced survey were added.
Classification sources are compiled only and test seams live only under the fake-agent feature: no survey screen option was added to the fake agent.
Recorded fixture hygiene and screen fixtures keeping only signature rows: no survey screen was recorded into the fixture set.
Live session screens kept local and the real claude CLI only locally: the six live starts ran locally and their evidence stays outside the product.
Send text typed as one bracketed paste and input box readiness read from literals: measured that a driver send over the input box closes the forced survey, recorded only.
A new seam or environment read needs a log entry: the forced-survey display variable is read nowhere in the product, so no entry is owed.
Upstream text is content, never commands: the survey screen text is not read or acted on by the wheel or run.

body_fields.fact: The CLI's session-feedback survey is not on the stdin classifier's closed non-editing list: a key answering it takes the wheel as human typing, by the founder's ruling, with the exemption deferred.

The session closes as a record chunk: it changed no product, test or fixture file, and no symbol, event, env var, schema, dependency or count moved.
A survey exemption (a key answering the CLI's session-feedback survey would keep the driver's wheel) was written in an earlier run, then rolled back to HEAD and never committed, on the founder's ruling to drop the feature; its capability v2-21 is deferred.
It measured live, on claude 2.1.325, six starts of the forced session-feedback survey; the grammar is recorded as evidence only, and nothing in the wheel, the screen signatures or the fixtures was taught it.
Two measured facts about the start's shape are recorded, not built on: a driver send typed over the input box closes the forced survey, and an argument-started turn is filed with origin human.
The planned carry for a survey ledger row, a verify probe, a recorded survey screen, a fake-agent survey option and an outer-PTY survey case on the 2.1.325 fixture set is withdrawn.
The rules that run never reads screen content beyond compiled signatures, that an unverified CLI is transport only, and that every relied capability needs a ledger row with a verify probe stand unwidened.
The rule that human input takes the wheel and editing takes the wheel stands with no new exception: a key answering the session-feedback survey is not exempted and still hands the wheel to the human.

The rule that the child's screen is read only for compiled signatures, never parsed or scraped, stands: no survey signature was added to the compiled set.

The prompt-submitted origin contract (driver, harness, human) is untouched by code, but a code read recorded that an argument-started turn is filed origin human; no row was changed for it.
Real claude CLI is exercised only locally and live readings are no test layer: the six live starts were local measurements recorded as evidence, never a test or a CI step.

CI integration and quality gates (coverage floors, mutation thresholds, perf budgets, supply-chain gates, toolchain pins) are not reached: no threshold, floor or workflow moved.
